annotations.text:
The settled proposal, drawn a few ways.

Words: sign up / log in, guest / signed in. The mechanics stay the transition; sign up is the story, and the card says what it keeps. Claim vocabulary is gone.

The career is totals and says so by saying nothing: no season, no week. Rating, tier, record, games are one meta call; rivets is already on the client.

The reroll lives behind NEW NAME on every board.

Two shapes are still open, so each is drawn twice: where the sign-up act sits on the page (keys in the head, or a foot key), and how loud the drawer banner is (a band, or one line).

THE GUEST PAGE, TWO WAYS.

Keys in the head (left, leading): the act sits beside the identity it acts on, and the claimed page is the same drawing with different keys, so the page keeps one shape across states.

Foot key (right): the menu's big-act grammar, DEPLOY and SAVE. Strongest possible sign-up, and the career sits between you and it as the argument. But the banner already carries the loud call, and a page with a lit foot key AND a banner elsewhere is the same voice twice; log in also ends up as small print, which it does not deserve on a shared machine.

THE BANNER, TWO WAYS. Shown once a guest has something to lose: an upgrade bought, a friend made, a rating banked. Before that it stays away, because a warning over an empty account is nagging. It rides every tab except the pilot page, which carries the act itself; pressing it goes there. The gold dot on the pilot stop is the permanent, quiet half of the reminder and stays either way.

The band (left, leading): the caution color at the menu's usual weights, standing on the rail where a thumb passes. Findable is its job.

One line (right): the same words at whisper. Calmer, and easy to never see, which is how pilots get lost.
The sign-up card. One field, and the note is the transition promise: keeps Delta 154 and everything it has flown. Log in stays its own card, unchanged but for the head.
